name: Ser Oswin
epithet: A knight of the Fourth Lance
appearance: A big, fair knight of the Fourth Lance, red to the cheekbones, with very blue eyes and big open hands; he wears the Fourth's green under a travelling cloak thrown back, sleeves rolled in a cold room, and warmth comes off him in lamplight as off a horse that has been ridden hard.
last_seen_doing: Heard Darrow's ford and said he would think on it, and drank to the river; knelt at the crossroads stone at first light; told Darrow the river was never the stone's fault; gave his word not to say where he met him; rode off down the Holloway toward the landing.
now: Gone down the Holloway toward the landing at a trot, his word given.
story_so_far: A big, warm knight of the Fourth who kneels at every stone the road gives him, Oswin knew the Captain by the stick and the face and sat down to play him rather than name him. He lifted a cart off a carter's boy with hands that came away white, asked Darrow to kneel beside him at the crossroads stone, heard Darrow's own ford in answer, knelt alone at first light, gave his word of silence and rode on.

quote.text: It's one knee. I'd kneel beside you. I'd be glad to.

known_facts.fact: He knew Darrow by the stick and the face from the writ on the bell-house door, and said he would not give him to a herald, a grey cloak or his own captain.
He kneels at every stone the road gives him, every morning since midsummer, and says he has not been cold or tired since.
He lifted a loaded cart off a pinned boy by himself, and his hands came away white to the wrist with frost, which was less and then gone without melting.
He believes the Lances at the ford lost the Grace because they had not knelt enough.
He asked Darrow to kneel beside him at the crossroads stone at first light and be what he was.
known_facts.evidence: It's one knee. I'd kneel beside you.

known_facts.fact: Told by Darrow that the warmth went out of him at the ford though he had knelt, he said it was a hard thing to be told over a cup and he would think on it.
known_facts.evidence: That's a hard thing to be told over a cup

known_facts.fact: He knelt at the crossroads stone at first light, and the frost went off the stone under his palms and off the ground under his knee.
known_facts.evidence: off the ground in one the shape of a knee

known_facts.fact: He gave Darrow his word not to say where he met him, nor to whom.
known_facts.evidence: I'll not say where I met you, nor to whom.

relationships.label: knew his face from the bell-house door
relationships.note: Lost to him at knucklebones, kept his name from the heralds, and asked him to kneel beside him at the crossroads stone.
